arm_tuning_capture.description:
Start a capture and optional budget override, then verify the real rate.

    ``rate_hz`` overrides the profile's own target for this capture only —
    the saved profile is untouched, so a one-off fast pull cannot quietly
    become the profile's normal.

    ``bus_budget_requests_per_second`` matters because demand and budget are
    two different knobs: raising the rate without the budget just queues, and
    raising the budget without the rate does *nothing at all* (measured
    2026-08-04 — 8 → 30 req/s moved the achieved rate not at all, because
    per-channel demand was capped at 1 Hz). Set both.

    After ``verify_seconds`` the capture is scored against its profile's
    contract and the response carries a ``verdict``: ``pass``, ``degraded``
    (gaps only, every channel >= 90 % covered), ``fail``, or ``unverified``.
    **Read the verdict before driving.** A ``fail`` names the
    clause and the fix in ``rate_verification.failures``; re-arm with the
    correction rather than starting the drive, because none of these problems
    are recoverable afterwards.

    Per-channel ``status`` separates the ways a capture disappoints, because
    they have opposite responses: ``shortfall`` means the achieved cadence
    fell below the requested rate, ``gap`` means the cadence was fine but the
    channel went quiet for a stretch (Mode 22 window closed, engine off, ECU
    stopped answering — see ``coverage.max_gap_s``), and ``missing`` means
    the ECU never answered at all, which wants the channel removed from the
    profile. The verdict names the constraint that actually bound
    (``failing_constraints``: unanswered_input, rate_shortfall,
    acquisition_gap, tuple_incomplete, tuple_skew, persistence_loss,
    unknown_loss_counters) with its evidence; it never prescribes a budget
    or rate change, because an old drop incident is not proof of the
    current limiting resource.

    ``tuples`` is the block to read for a fuelling capture: ``complete`` is
    the number of rounds in which every ``required_tuple`` member was
    persisted within the profile's ``max_tuple_skew_s``, counted from the
    rows on disk. ``tuple_rate_bound_hz`` is only a bound (the slowest
    member's cadence). A capture whose channels all read healthy still
    yields nothing if the tuple never completes.

    The verdict is scoped: ``scope: live`` covers arm to now, on what has
    been persisted so far, and reports capture-scoped ``achieved_hz`` beside
    the ``observed_seconds`` it was measured over. A shortfall against
    ``rate_hz`` means demand exceeded the budget — throttling working, not a
    fault. Pass ``verify_seconds=0`` to skip the wait and
    return immediately — the verdict is then absent rather than assumed good.
arm_tuning_capture.name: arm_tuning_capture

can_activity.description:
Capture N seconds of raw CAN traffic; per-ID frame rate + which byte
    positions changed.

    The RE workhorse: call it bracketing a physical action (press the brake,
    flip a switch — tag what you *did*, per AGENTS.md's "tag physical
    actions, not screen selections" convention) and `changed_byte_indices`
    on each id is the answer to "which ID carries that signal," without an
    offline candump-and-diff round trip. Pure listen — no CAN frames are
    transmitted, so this has no interaction with passive mode.

    `ids` restricts the capture to those arbitration ids (useful for a
    follow-up call once a wide capture has narrowed the candidates); omit
    for the whole bus. `seconds` is capped at 30 server-side.
can_activity.name: can_activity

cancel_job.description: Best-effort cancellation. Already-finished jobs are a no-op.
cancel_job.name: cancel_job

classify_session.description:
Run the classifier on ``session_id`` and persist the sidecar.

    Returns the new classification payload (same shape as
    :func:`get_session_classification`). Re-running on a session with
    an existing sidecar overwrites — the classifier is deterministic
    given the same inputs, so re-runs are safe and useful when the
    classifier_version has been bumped.
classify_session.name: classify_session

compare_tuning_sessions.description:
A/B two stored sessions on a matched grid (local). Refuses
            calculated load as an axis — it is derived from BFS, so it moves
            when fuelling moves; grid on rpm x MAF or rpm x BFS. Pass
            ``floor_channel`` with ``conditions`` (the regime this comparison
            was made under) to quote each delta against the measured same-tune
            noise floor, below which nothing is distinguishable; a floor
            measured under other conditions is refused, not quoted.
compare_tuning_sessions.name: compare_tuning_sessions

diff_did_snapshots.description:
Diff two completed ``did_sweep`` job results.

    Reuses ``classify_dids`` (the same classifier ``tools/scan_constant_dids.py``
    uses across passes at different engine states) on exactly two snapshots:
    `varying` = DIDs whose value differs between the two runs — the
    candidates worth investigating; `constant` = answered in both, same
    value both times; `intermittent` = answered in one run but not the other
    (a session/timing flake, or a DID gated on the condition itself). Each
    entry carries the raw hex from each snapshot it appeared in — the
    codebase has no scale/offset for most DIDs yet, so raw bytes are the
    honest thing to hand back.
diff_did_snapshots.name: diff_did_snapshots

disarm_tuning_capture.description:
Stop the active capture and put the bus budget back.

    Stopping restores exactly the override that was in force before capture.
    ``clear_bus_budget`` is an explicit request to discard that restored
    operator setting. The response includes the ended session directory, so
    it can be analysed without hunting for it (capture sessions are
    ``_``-prefixed and deliberately invisible to the normal session listing).
disarm_tuning_capture.name: disarm_tuning_capture

estimate_tuning.description:
Before/after FP estimate for a proposed config, no state change.

    Audited anyway because seeing what was modeled is useful — the
    ``result="ok"`` entry includes the proposed config and the daemon's
    response.
estimate_tuning.name: estimate_tuning

get_behavior_deviations.description:
Diff a stored session against the learned behavior surfaces (local,
            no daemon HTTP call) — did a mod/retrain/change actually move behavior?
            Pass ``against`` to A/B ``session`` directly against a second session
            id instead (Task 5.4: before-mod vs. after-mod, session-to-session).
get_behavior_deviations.name: get_behavior_deviations

get_behavior_live.description:
Live ``you-are-here`` overlay for the behavior surfaces.

    Returns per-model ``expected`` / ``actual`` / ``deviation`` / ``severity``
    for the most recent tick. ``include_series=True`` also returns each
    model's rolling trail (~4 min at 1 Hz) — the default is ``False`` because
    with enough registered surfaces the full trail can exceed the MCP
    tool-result size cap; pass ``True`` only when you actually need the
    trajectory (e.g. plotting a Δ sparkline), not for a one-shot status check.
    Equivalent to ``GET /models/behavior/live?series=...`` — see
    :mod:`src.dashboard.behavior_live` for the schema.
get_behavior_live.name: get_behavior_live

get_behavior_models.description:
Static behavior surfaces (the learned "normal" maps).

    1D/2D surfaces over operating-mode-segmented data. Use this with
    ``get_behavior_live`` to compare "where the engine should be" with
    "where it is right now."
get_behavior_models.name: get_behavior_models

get_bindings.description:
Decoded CAN signal metadata — ``data/bindings.yaml`` as JSON.

    The daemon re-reads on every request, so an edit during reverse
    engineering shows up here without restart.
get_bindings.name: get_bindings

get_binned_analysis.description:
Bin a value channel by an x (and optional y) channel over a
        session/date scope — "trims by rpm×load" without hand-written SQL
        or a refit (Task 5.1). ``agg``: mean/median/p95/count.
get_binned_analysis.name: get_binned_analysis

get_capture_quality.description:
The capture contract verdict: live for the active capture, or recomputed.

    Without ``session_id`` this is the running capture scored on what has
    been persisted so far (``scope: live``). With one, the daemon recomputes
    coverage and tuple yield from that session's rows without rewriting it
    and returns the stored sidecar beside the recomputation — a v1 sidecar
    comes back as ``scope: trailing_snapshot`` with losses unknown, which is
    what it was. Read ``failures[].clause`` for the constraint that bound
    (unanswered_input, rate_shortfall, acquisition_gap, tuple_incomplete,
    tuple_skew, persistence_loss, unknown_loss_counters); ``losses`` is
    scoped to the capture or marked unknown, never assumed zero.
get_capture_quality.name: get_capture_quality

get_config.description:
Echo of the daemon's loaded ``canary.yaml`` as JSON.

    Useful when a tuning or threshold question depends on the configured
    operating-mode boundaries, sample rate, retention, etc.
get_config.name: get_config

get_corpus_mode_summary.description:
Aggregate mode-coverage + event counts across every classified session.

    Useful for "do I have enough warmup data to retrain the
    coolant_warmup behavior model?" — the answer is in
    ``mode_seconds.warmup`` and ``event_counts.cold_start``.
get_corpus_mode_summary.name: get_corpus_mode_summary

get_current_capture.description:
Read the currently active capture window (pure read).

    ``active`` is the field to check: with no window open this answers 200
    with ``capture: null``, ``active: false`` and a ``detail`` naming the
    cause (a daemon restart drops the in-memory window while recording
    continues). Do not read a null ``capture`` as "the call failed" or as
    "a window is open" — it is neither.
get_current_capture.name: get_current_capture

get_dataset_health.description:
Corpus readiness: per-mode sample counts, gaps, last-seen times.

    Useful when deciding whether retraining now is worthwhile.
get_dataset_health.name: get_dataset_health

get_delivery_error.description:
Measured-vs-commanded AFR at enrichment for one stored session,
            with the methodology gates applied and reported (local, no daemon
            call). Closed-loop samples and decel fuel cut are excluded by
            construction, and results are band-averaged over rpm so uneven
            coverage cannot masquerade as an effect. ``measured_spec`` is
            explicit because the ECM lambda and A/F-voltage paths disagree by
            ~3.8% at WOT and neither is established as truth.
get_delivery_error.name: get_delivery_error

get_dids.description:
Nissan Mode-22 DID catalog (schema_version + per-DID entries).

    Returns an empty doc if the catalog file isn't present.
get_dids.name: get_dids

get_dtc.description:
Cached stored/pending/permanent DTC report and MIL state.

    Mirrors ``GET /obd/dtc`` on the dashboard: the periodic Mode 03/07/0A
    poll's latest snapshot, with `description`/`system` per code, `mil_on`,
    `captured_at`, and a `stale` flag when the poll hasn't refreshed recently
    (or no poll has landed yet). Read-only — there is no clear-codes tool.
get_dtc.name: get_dtc

get_feedback.description: All recorded operator feedback labels + summary counts.
get_feedback.name: get_feedback

get_job.description: Status + result payload for a single job.
get_job.name: get_job

get_job_logs.description: Captured stdout/stderr of a job (full log; the daemon doesn't paginate).
get_job_logs.name: get_job_logs

get_monitors.description:
Cached Mode 06 on-board monitor sweep: per-cylinder misfire counts and
    raw monitor test results (value/min/max, pass/fail).

    Mirrors ``GET /obd/monitors`` on the dashboard: the periodic Mode 06
    poll's latest snapshot (Task 3.1), with a `stale` flag when the poll
    hasn't refreshed recently (or no poll has landed yet). Read-only.
get_monitors.name: get_monitors

get_obd_coverage.description:
Honesty surface for OBD coverage.

    Lists which standard PIDs the ECU supports, which CANary decodes, and
    which are gaps — useful when debugging "why don't I see X?"
get_obd_coverage.name: get_obd_coverage

get_power_status.description:
UPS (X1202) power state: SoC, cell voltage, watchdog armed/on-battery/
    seconds-on-battery/grace window, and any active keep-alive hold.

    Mirrors ``GET /control/power``. Use this instead of SSH'ing into the Pi to
    check the watchdog when the dashboard is unreachable — a bench Pi shows
    ``on_battery: false`` (external power confirmed); a real key-off shows
    ``seconds_lost`` counting up toward ``grace_s``. ``watchdog_running: false``
    means the ``ups-shutdown`` service isn't up (or its status file is stale —
    check ``watchdog_stale``), not necessarily a power problem.
get_power_status.name: get_power_status

get_recent_anomalies.description:
Anomaly events from the JSONL log, newest ``limit`` returned oldest-first.

    Parameters
    ----------
    since:
        ISO-8601 timestamp; the daemon returns events with timestamp >= since
        and skips daily log files dated more than a day before it. ``None``
        applies no time bound: the daemon walks the log newest-day-first
        until it has ``limit`` events.
    limit:
        Newest N events, sent to the daemon so it stops reading early. ``0``
        or less removes the cap, and with no ``since`` that parses the whole
        anomaly history inside the collecting daemon.
    source:
        ``"isolation_forest"`` or ``"lstm_autoencoder"`` to filter by detector.
        Applied by the daemon before ``limit`` counts.
    mode:
        Operating mode (``idle``, ``city``, ``highway``, ``wot``, ``off_road``)
        to filter by — useful when a problem only appears in one regime.
        Applied by the daemon before ``limit`` counts.
get_recent_anomalies.name: get_recent_anomalies

get_recent_telemetry.description:
The last ``n`` rows from the newest session.

    Returns rows in the daemon's long-format schema: ``timestamp``, ``source``,
    ``channel``, ``value_number`` / ``value_text`` / ``value_bool``, ``unit``,
    plus metadata. Set ``per_channel=True`` to get one latest row per channel
    (a state snapshot) instead of the last ``n`` records globally. ``channel``
    is a client-side filter applied after fetch.
get_recent_telemetry.name: get_recent_telemetry

get_replay_status.description:
Return the current live-replay state: idle or running, source session,
    output paths and emission counters (pure read, no audit).
get_replay_status.name: get_replay_status

get_service_health.description:
systemctl health (active/restart-count/uptime) for canary, canary-mcp,
        ups-shutdown — the crash-loop tell without SSH.
get_service_health.name: get_service_health

get_session.description: Detail for one session: tags, control.json, chunk count, metadata.
get_session.name: get_session

get_session_classification.description:
Modes + events + disposition sidecar for one session.

    Returns ``404`` (raised as :class:`DaemonError`) when the session has
    no sidecar yet — call :func:`classify_session` (write tool) or run
    ``scripts/label_sessions.py`` to generate it.
get_session_classification.name: get_session_classification

get_session_digest.description:
End-of-drive digest for one session: duration, mode seconds, gated
    anomaly counts by source, top behavior-surface deviations, fingerprint
    deltas vs. the frozen reference epoch, new DTCs, and new vehicle-ledger
    events.

    Written by the trip-end hook (Task 5.4 — sustained GPS stop, or daemon
    shutdown as a fallback); computed on demand and cached if that hook
    hasn't fired yet for this session. Two distinct failures, both raised as
    :class:`~src.mcp_server.client.DaemonError` — read the status, they mean
    opposite things:

    * **404** — the session id doesn't resolve, or has no telemetry
      recorded. Nothing was attempted.
    * **409** — the digest was *refused*, and the body's ``digest_skipped``
      block says why (D03.6): more rows than ``daemon.digest_row_budget``,
      a directory that is not a session (``_replay-*``), or a child that hit
      its address-space ceiling. That is a fact about the session, not a
      missing sidecar — do not retry it expecting a different answer.

    Authenticated (auth-consistency follow-up to Task 5.6): the digest
    aggregates the vehicle ledger and per-session fingerprint z-scores,
    both otherwise only readable via authenticated ``/control/*`` routes
    (``list_vehicle_events`` / ``get_trends``) — ``client`` must carry the
    control token, same as those tools.
get_session_digest.name: get_session_digest

get_session_timeseries.description:
Aligned historical channels from a Pi session, without SSH/export.

        Use ``source:CHANNEL`` names such as ``obd:RPM`` and
        ``obd:ENGINE_LOAD``. One Hz is appropriate for a whole drive; use a
        higher rate only when resolving a short transient.
get_session_timeseries.name: get_session_timeseries

get_status.description:
Snapshot of daemon liveness, loaded models, storage, and emitter counters.

    Mirrors ``GET /status`` on the dashboard. Use this first when debugging
    "is the pipeline alive?" — it tells you storage path / free MB, the latest
    session id, model versions loaded, anomaly emitter counters, and (when the
    daemon has wired one in) the inference-health block (latency, freshness,
    missing-feature rate, drift).

    ``view="compact"`` returns the pollable projection instead: measured
    ~4 ms / 1.3 KB against ~42 ms / 26 KB for the full payload on the dev
    laptop, and the full payload takes 1.3–2.6 s on the Pi. It carries
    ``vehicle_state`` plus the counters a watchdog acts on — per-sink
    ``dropped_records`` and queue depth/high-water, ``can0``, the inference
    tick/miss counters, OBD request/response/timeout totals, ``capture_profile``
    name + active, ``passive``, ``free_mb`` and ``health.system`` — each at the
    same path it occupies in the full payload, and stamped with ``served_at``.
    Use it for any repeated poll, and for bracketing a counter measurement.
    Take the full view when you need per-channel rates, the request table,
    discovery, model provenance or GPS.
get_status.name: get_status

get_training_runs.description: Training-run history (the latest record per run from the ledger).
get_training_runs.name: get_training_runs

get_trends.description:
Per-stat drift trend over the fingerprint history: latest value,
    reference band, Mann-Kendall trend verdict, CUSUM alarm state.

    ``available: false`` (with a ``reason``) when no reference epoch has
    been frozen yet (``scripts/fingerprint.py freeze``) — there's nothing to
    trend against.
get_trends.name: get_trends

get_trip_summary.description:
Trip-summary sidecar for one session: duration, distance, fuel used,
    average economy, CO2, idle time/fraction, max/avg speed, 0-60 and
    1/4-mile if a clean launch was captured.

    Computed on demand from the stored session (Task 1.4 — there is no
    session-close hook yet) and cached to ``trip_summary.json`` after the
    first request. 404 (raised as :class:`~src.mcp_server.client.DaemonError`)
    when the session id doesn't resolve or has no telemetry recorded.
get_trip_summary.name: get_trip_summary

get_tuning.description: Currently active alert-tuning config (thresholds, dedupe, etc.).
get_tuning.name: get_tuning

list_capture_profiles.description: List the active vehicle's saved collection profiles.
list_capture_profiles.name: list_capture_profiles

list_events_by_kind.description:
Corpus-wide search through every session's ``derived_tags.jsonl``.

    ``kind`` filters to events of one type (``hard_accel``, ``cold_start``,
    ``cruise``, etc.); ``None`` returns all kinds. Results are newest-first
    and capped at ``limit``.
list_events_by_kind.name: list_events_by_kind

list_jobs.description: All known jobs (queued, running, completed, failed).
list_jobs.name: list_jobs

list_sessions.description:
All known sessions on disk, oldest-first.

    ``since`` / ``until`` bound the listing by ISO session start time and
    ``limit`` keeps only the newest N. Use this for navigation; combine with
    ``get_session`` to drill into one.
list_sessions.name: list_sessions

list_vehicle_events.description:
Every vehicle ledger entry, oldest-first (latest per id — corrections
    collapsed, but nothing lost from the on-disk append-only chain).

    Use this to check what's already logged before recording a duplicate, or
    to correlate an anomaly's timestamp against nearby maintenance/mods.
list_vehicle_events.name: list_vehicle_events

obd_request.description:
One-shot OBD/UDS request against the live ECU(s).

    ``service`` takes any service byte — read, write and actuation alike.
    Nothing filters it, so a Mode 04 or a UDS 0x2E/0x2F goes out exactly as
    asked; the caller decides what is appropriate to send. For the ordinary
    read services this just lets you ask for one specific service/identifier
    combination immediately instead of waiting for the poll scheduler's
    cadence (Mode 06 and DTC sit on a 5-minute tier).

    ``identifier`` is the PID/DID/MID/InfoType byte(s) — omit it for the
    no-identifier services (Mode 03/07/0A). ``header`` overrides the default
    functional request id (``0x7DF``) for a physically-addressed request,
    e.g. ``0x7E0`` for the engine ECM, or another module's tester address —
    set it to reach a module standard Mode 01 polling never does (ABS,
    TCM, ...).

    Returns ``responded: false`` (not an error) when nothing answers in
    time — a real "unsupported" for this ECU is indistinguishable on the
    wire from a request that simply timed out. When another tool owns a
    diagnostic session with a module, arm ``set_passive_mode`` first so this
    request's own transmit can't contend with it.
obd_request.name: obd_request

pin_session.description:
Pin a session as a training candidate / interesting-to-keep record.

    ``reason`` and optional ``metadata`` end up in the session's record. Pinned
    sessions survive retention sweeps.
pin_session.name: pin_session

query_telemetry.description:
Run a single SELECT/WITH against the telemetry Parquet view.

            View name is `telemetry` with columns timestamp, source, channel,
            value_number, value_text, value_bool, unit, metadata_json, and a
            derived `session` column. Non-SELECT statements are rejected.
            session/since/until scope which sessions' parquet back the view
            for this call (cheaper than scanning the whole corpus) — since/
            until are ISO-8601 or a bare session id, inclusive both ends.
query_telemetry.name: query_telemetry

record_feedback.description:
Record true_positive/false_positive/unknown verdict on an anomaly.

        Pass the whole `event` dict straight through from
        `get_recent_anomalies` — the store keys on the event, and these
        events have no id field.
record_feedback.name: record_feedback

record_vehicle_event.description:
Log a maintenance/mod/repair/observation to the vehicle ledger (3.3).

        ``occurred_at`` is an ISO date (``YYYY-MM-DD``). Set
        ``corpus_boundary=True`` when the event changes what "normal" looks
        like (a mod or repair) so training can optionally start fresh from
        it (``--since-boundary``).

        Pass ``event_id`` (from `list_vehicle_events`) to CORRECT an existing
        entry: the ledger is append-only and reads collapse to the latest
        line per id, so the correction wins while the original stays on
        disk. Re-state the whole event, not just the changed field.
record_vehicle_event.name: record_vehicle_event

replay_window.description:
Submit a ``replay_window`` job; optionally wait + return the report.

    Parameters
    ----------
    session_id:
        Session directory name (e.g. ``"2026-05-17T120000"``).
    start / end:
        Optional ISO-8601 bounds (inclusive). Omitted bounds replay the
        whole session.
    if_model / lstm_model:
        Optional artifact path overrides; defaults follow ``canary.yaml``.
    anomalies_dir:
        Optional override for where to look up historical events.
    max_rows / max_windows:
        Caps on the per-row IF score list and per-window LSTM list to keep
        the JSON response bounded; defaults are 5000 each.
    wait:
        Block until the job terminates (default). When ``False``, returns
        the queued ``JobRecord`` and the caller polls ``get_job`` /
        ``get_job_logs`` themselves.
    poll_interval / timeout:
        Polling cadence and overall wall-clock cap when ``wait=True``.

    Returns
    -------
    On success and ``wait=True``: ``{"ok": True, "job": {...}, "report": {...}}``.
    On ``wait=False``: ``{"ok": True, "job": {...}, "report": None}``.
    On failure: ``{"ok": False, "job": {...}, "error": "..."}``.
replay_window.name: replay_window

revert_tuning.description:
Revert to an earlier tuning version (from the audit log).

    Reverting is itself a new, audited version — the audit chain is
    append-only and never rewinds.
revert_tuning.name: revert_tuning

search_anomaly_log.description:
Search anomaly history (kind='anomalies') or the MCP audit log (kind='audit').

        Anomaly filters: source (isolation_forest|lstm_autoencoder), mode,
        min_score / max_score, affected_channel, session. Audit filters:
        action (e.g. 'mcp.start_capture'), result ('ok'|'error'), actor.
        ``contains`` does a raw-text substring match for fields outside the
        structured filters. Results are newest-first, capped at ``limit``.
search_anomaly_log.name: search_anomaly_log

set_bus_budget.description:
Raise (or clear) the OBD request-rate budget for a bounded capture.

    The scheduler paces at ``BUS_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER x poll_rate_hz`` — 8
    requests/second on the dev vehicle — against a measured capability of
    **667 single-PID reads/s**. That conservatism is why a WOT pull yields
    ~23 usable samples where UpRev's K-line logger gets 537, and why AFR and
    Load Point Scaler work has repeatedly had to borrow that external tool.

    Raise it for the pull, drop it after. Pass ``requests_per_second=None``
    to clear and return to the configured default.

    Pairs with ``set_tuning_mode``: narrowing the channel set concentrates
    the budget, raising the budget enlarges it. For WOT work you generally
    want both — but note tuning mode also suspends the Mode-22 DID windows,
    so leave it off if you need DIDs (e.g. ``DID_1208`` injector pulse width)
    during the same drive.

    ``ttl_seconds`` **defaults to 600** rather than to off, unlike
    ``set_passive_mode``. A forgotten passive mode is loud — nothing gets
    logged. A forgotten rate override is quiet: it just keeps hammering the
    bus and burning Pi CPU at up to 25x the intended rate indefinitely. Pass
    ``None`` only if you deliberately want it to persist.

    Ceiling is 200 req/s, well under the measured 667: that figure came from
    a probe with the bus effectively to itself, whereas in service it also
    carries ~29 broadcast IDs on 9-18 ms cadences. Raising the budget also
    stops helping once responses can't keep up — watch ``response_rate`` in
    ``get_status``, and if it drops, the extra requests are just bus noise.
    ``get_status`` reports ``bus_budget`` (override, source, TTL remaining)
    so an unexpectedly high achieved rate is distinguishable from a fault.
set_bus_budget.name: set_bus_budget

set_passive_mode.description:
Arm (``enabled=true``) or disarm the CAN transmit gate.

    While armed the daemon is receive-only: broadcast CAN logging, telemetry
    storage, GPS and anomaly scoring all keep running, but no OBD polls and no
    ISO-TP flow-control frames are transmitted.

    Arm this whenever another tool owns a diagnostic session with a module —
    ECU reprogramming, a bidirectional actuator test, a scan-tool routine —
    so CANary's polling cannot contend with it.

    ``ttl_seconds`` (only meaningful when arming, capped at 3600) auto-disarms
    after that many seconds even if nobody calls this again — the daemon
    polls for expiry in the background. Worth setting whenever the window is
    known in advance (a timed reflash, a fixed-length scan-tool routine): it
    is one less thing to remember, and a died session or an interrupted
    conversation can't leave OBD polling suppressed indefinitely. Omit for
    the old "stays armed until manually disarmed" behavior.

    Note that OBD channels go stale while armed, so ``vehicle_state`` will
    read ``engine_off``/``no_data`` and behavior models will stop scoring. That
    is expected, not a fault; ``get_status`` reports ``passive.enabled`` (and
    ``passive.ttl_remaining_seconds`` when a TTL is set) so both are
    distinguishable from a real fault. Disarm when the other tool is
    finished, or let the TTL do it.

    For a guarantee no software path can defeat, additionally put the
    controller in listen-only mode on the Pi (``ip link set can0 type can
    listen-only on``) — that requires an interface cycle and cannot be done
    through this tool.
set_passive_mode.name: set_passive_mode

set_session_metadata.description:
Attach / merge metadata onto a session.

    ``merge=True`` (default) shallow-merges with existing metadata; ``False``
    replaces. The daemon's REST endpoint uses these same semantics.
set_session_metadata.name: set_session_metadata

set_tuning.description:
Replace the alert-tuning config. The daemon auto-bumps ``version``.

    Run ``estimate_tuning`` first to preview the false-positive impact over
    recent anomalies — the daemon writes every change to an audit log so
    everything is revertible.
set_tuning.name: set_tuning

set_tuning_mode.description:
Arm/disarm the focused high-rate tuning poll profile.

    While armed the Mode 01 rotation is restricted to a small tuning set
    (RPM, load, MAF, timing, TPS, IAT, lambda B1/B2, STFT/LTFT B1/B2,
    commanded equivalence ratio) and the Mode-22 DID windows are suspended,
    so each channel gets a far larger slice of the same bus budget.

    Use for a tuning capture where you need enough samples in a single
    rpm x load cell to draw a conclusion. Normal polling lands each channel
    at 0.06-0.5 Hz, which yields roughly 10 samples per cell over a whole
    drive -- not enough to say anything.

    Everything outside the tuning set stops updating while armed. That is
    expected, not a fault; `get_status` reports `tuning_mode.active`.
    Disarm when the capture is done -- disabling also restores the default
    channel set, so a narrow one-off cannot persist into the next capture.
set_tuning_mode.name: set_tuning_mode

set_ups_keepalive.description:
Set (``minutes`` > 0) or cancel (``minutes`` = 0) the UPS keep-alive hold.

    Use before a bench move longer than the watchdog's grace window (default
    5 min) — e.g. unplugging to carry the Pi somewhere for an extended
    session. While the hold is active the watchdog will not power off
    regardless of input/battery state. It expires on its own; there's no need
    to explicitly cancel unless you want the grace-window protection back
    immediately.
set_ups_keepalive.name: set_ups_keepalive

signal_lookup.description:
Fuzzy-match a tag label against the FSM signal catalog.

            ``can_id`` narrows the search to that module (e.g. 0x7E0 → ECM)
            for better precision. Returns top-k name matches with scores.
signal_lookup.name: signal_lookup

start_capture.description:
Start a named capture profile or a legacy labeled capture window.

        Pass ``profile`` for an isolated collection session. Without it,
        ``purpose`` starts the existing tag window on the current session.
start_capture.name: start_capture

start_job.description:
Submit a job to the daemon's controller.

    Common ``kind`` values: ``corpus_report``, ``retrain_if``, ``retrain_lstm``,
    ``did_sweep``. See ``src/control/jobs.py`` for the registered set on this
    build.

    ``did_sweep`` sweeps a Mode 22 DID range in one pass: params
    ``{start, end, label}`` required (``start``/``end`` are DIDs, int or hex
    string; ``label`` tags the snapshot for ``diff_did_snapshots``), optional
    ``header``/``session``/``keepalive``/``delay_seconds``/``read_timeout`` —
    see ``diff_did_snapshots``'s docstring for the before/after workflow this
    feeds.
start_job.name: start_job

start_replay.description:
Replay a stored session into the live capture pipeline.

    Pushes the recorded session's telemetry onto the same queue as a real
    drive, so IF + LSTM + behavior detectors fire as if the truck were
    running. Parquet writes land under ``<storage>/_replay-<id>/`` and
    anomalies under ``<anomalies_dir>/_replay/<id>.jsonl`` — both
    excluded from training discovery and feedback loops.

    Parameters
    ----------
    session_id:
        Directory name of an existing live session (e.g.
        ``"2026-05-18T033527"``). Replay-of-replays is rejected.
    speed:
        Multiplier on the original recording's pacing. ``1.0`` real-time;
        ``3.0`` three times faster.
    loop:
        Loop the recording until ``stop_replay`` is called. Default
        ``False`` so the replay halts on its own when the source exhausts.
start_replay.name: start_replay

stop_capture.description:
Stop the active profile capture, otherwise close the tag window.

        Raises when there is no tag window to close (HTTP 409) rather than
        answering with a null capture — a restart drops the in-memory window,
        so "stopped" and "there was nothing to stop" are genuinely different
        answers. The refusal names that cause.
stop_capture.name: stop_capture

stop_replay.description: Cancel the in-flight replay and roll the writer/logger back to live.
stop_replay.name: stop_replay

tag_current_capture.description:
Drop a tag onto the active capture mid-drive.

    Tags are append-only events in ``tags.jsonl`` — used to mark transitions
    ("entered city", "started towing") so downstream analysis can slice.

    Raises :class:`~src.mcp_server.client.DaemonError` when no capture window
    is open (HTTP 409) — the tag was *not* recorded. The window is in-memory
    only, so a daemon restart ends it while recording continues; the refusal
    says so. Never returns a success with a null tag: a lost tag cannot be
    recovered after the drive, so it has to fail loudly at the call.
tag_current_capture.name: tag_current_capture

tail_daemon_log.description:
Recent daemon log lines as parsed JSON records.

        Reads from systemd journal when available; falls back to a flat log
        file at $CANARY_MCP_LOG_FALLBACK otherwise. ``unit`` overrides the
        default ($CANARY_MCP_DAEMON_UNIT, "canary").
tail_daemon_log.name: tail_daemon_log

trigger_poll.description:
Force specific channels due on the OBD scheduler's next tick.

    Nudges the poll scheduler instead of waiting out a channel's configured
    cadence — DTC/Mode 06 sit on a 5-minute tier, so this turns "wait up to
    5 minutes" into "the answer is ready in a few seconds." Channel names
    match `get_status`'s `obd_scheduler.requests[].channel` (`RPM`,
    `DTC_STORED`, `MONITOR_RESULTS`, `DID_1101`, ...), matched
    case-insensitively; an unknown name is silently never matched.

    This only queues the request — it does not wait for or return the
    reading. Read the result back a few seconds later with the usual tools
    (`get_status`, `get_dtc`, `get_recent_telemetry`, `query_telemetry`).
trigger_poll.name: trigger_poll

unpin_session.description: Remove the pin from a session — it's eligible for retention sweeps again.
unpin_session.name: unpin_session

upload_model_artifact.description:
Upload a trained model artifact (path local to the MCP host).

        ``artifact_path`` is read from the MCP server's filesystem,
        base64-encoded, and POSTed alongside ``manifest`` to
        ``/control/models/{model_type}/artifact``. Audited with file size +
        manifest; the base64 body itself is not logged.
upload_model_artifact.name: upload_model_artifact
